subject: Trading
title: Margin Calls and Forced Selling
description: One-minute skill: Margin Calls and Forced Selling.

hook.text: A trader borrows money to buy stocks. Prices drop. The broker demands more cash. The trader can't pay. Forced sale.

buildup.text: Margin calls happen when leveraged positions decline and the broker requires additional collateral immediately.

discovery.text: Forced selling from margin calls creates a feedback loop: selling pushes prices down, triggering more margin calls.

twist.text: In the 1929 crash, margin requirements were just 10%. A small dip wiped out millions of leveraged investors.

climax.text: Margin calls turn market declines into accelerating cascades. Leverage is the gasoline that feeds the fire.

quiz.question: How do margin calls worsen crashes?
options: Forced selling from calls pushes prices lower, triggering more calls
